title: Postgres via API: 10 user JSON files become rows that match the source
summary: Submits local (10 user JSON files) -> postgres table e2e_users through the API and checks the table against the source: rows equal the records the run reported, every file is represented, every row carries this run id, and a known email lands exactly once.

steps.title: Drop e2e_users
steps.explain: Starts clean so every row counted later was written by this run.

steps.title: Submit the job through the API
steps.explain: POST /api/v1/jobs with the TOML base64-encoded, exactly as the console does.

steps.title: Wait for the run to finish
steps.explain: Polls the task result and GET /api/v1/runs until this run reaches a terminal status.

steps.title: Run finished COMPLETED
steps.explain: A clean run must report COMPLETED, not PARTIAL or FAILED.

steps.title: Delivered equals records read
steps.explain: Every record the run read must be reported as delivered to the sink.

steps.title: No record failed
steps.explain: records_failed must be 0 on a clean run.

steps.title: The run read some records
steps.explain: A run that reads nothing proves nothing.

steps.title: Run read every source file
steps.explain: Files read must equal files on disk.

steps.title: Count rows in e2e_users
steps.explain: The real number of rows the sink wrote.

steps.title: Rows equal records reported
steps.explain: The table must hold exactly what the run says it delivered.

steps.title: Count distinct source files in the table
steps.explain: Every source file must be represented.

steps.title: Count rows stamped with this run id
steps.explain: Provenance: rows must say which run wrote them.

args.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM e2e_users WHERE job_run_id = '${run.run_id}'

steps.title: All rows carry this run id
steps.explain: Every row came from this run.

steps.title: Find the user Sincere@april.biz
steps.explain: Spot-check that real field values arrived.

args.sql: SELECT count(*) FROM e2e_users WHERE text LIKE '%Sincere@april.biz%'

steps.title: Exactly one row holds that email
steps.explain: The user is in the source once.

steps.title: Show sample rows
steps.explain: Evidence of what the rows contain.

args.sql: SELECT source_filename, element_type, left(text, 80) AS text FROM e2e_users ORDER BY source_filename LIMIT 5
